one_line: An artisan from the Mahajanapada age crafting early punch-marked silver karshapana coins in North India.

appearance.age_look: Mid-20s, lean but work-toned build, average height
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown North Indian complexion, straight nose, calm focused eyes with slightly thick brows, a faint hammer-callus scar on the left cheek, default expression a quiet, intent concentration as if judging silver weight.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair tied into a short topknot at the crown with the rest combed back and neatly trimmed at the nape, a simple narrow off-white cloth band wrapped once around the forehead as a sweatband.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate mid-Ganga plain artisan attire: a knee-length off-white cotton dhoti wrapped snugly and pleated in front with a plain brown woven belt cord, a short-sleeved light-indigo cotton upper cloth (like a simple kurta-tunic) reaching mid-thigh with a straight round neckline and side slits, and a soft un-dyed cotton angavastra shawl with a thin reddish-brown border draped over the left shoulder and under the right arm; simple leather sandals, a small copper earring in the left ear, and a narrow bronze bangle on the right wrist complete the look.
appearance.signature: A low rectangular stone coin-anvil slab with neatly aligned small silver pieces, held with his left hand, and in his right a short iron hammer with a wooden handle poised over a tiny square metal punch bearing a sun-like symbol, with a small cloth pouch of finished punch-marked karshapanas at his waist.

ref_desc: A mid-20s lean North Indian man with medium-brown complexion, black topknot hair and a forehead cloth band, wearing an off-white dhoti, light indigo tunic, reddish-brown bordered shawl and leather sandals, holding a stone anvil, hammer, sun-symbol punch and silver karshapana coins in off-white, indigo, brown and silver tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a mid-20s lean North Indian artisan from the 6th–4th century BCE, with medium-brown complexion, an oval face, calm focused eyes, a faint hammer-callus scar on his left cheek, and thick black hair pulled into a short topknot with the rest neatly trimmed and a narrow off-white cloth band around his forehead; dress him in a historically plausible mid-Ganga plain outfit: a knee-length off-white cotton dhoti wrapped and pleated at the front with a plain brown woven cord belt, a short-sleeved light indigo cotton tunic reaching mid-thigh with a simple round neck and side slits, and an un-dyed cotton angavastra shawl with a thin reddish-brown border draped over his left shoulder and under his right arm, plus simple leather sandals, a small copper earring in his left ear, and a narrow bronze bangle on his right wrist; place in his hands his signature tools: a low rectangular stone coin-anvil slab with aligned small silver pieces held in his left hand, and in his right a short iron hammer with a wooden handle raised over a tiny square metal punch engraved with a sun-like symbol, with a small cloth pouch of finished punch-marked silver karshapana coins tied at his waist; use a palette dominated by off-white, light indigo blue, reddish-brown, warm brown and silver, and present front, side and back poses plus a close-up of his face and his hammer-punch-and-anvil set to clearly show his consistent design.
